column1: # manifest-map.tsv: the ONLY non-default resolution rules of run4/evidence/verify-manifests.sh. Columns are TAB-separated:
# `manifest` is relative to docs/v2/evidence/remediation-20261114/ (the "BASE"). Paths in args are BASE-relative unless stated.
# DEFAULT (no row): an entry resolves to <manifest directory>/<entry> (leading `*` and `./` removed) in the committed tree at REV,
#   and, when the entry is an absolute path under the read-only allow-list, to that host path. Nothing is ever searched for by basename or suffix.
#   include   M  -  -        M is a hash list whose name does not match the manifest name rule; treat it as a manifest
#   format    M  hash-path | hash-bytes-path | hash-marker-path   (default hash-path; marker = the literal word host-only)
#   croot     M  <BASE-rel root>|@|-   committed root(s) tried as <root>/<entry>; `@` = the manifest's directory (the default); `-` = none
#   hroot     M  <absolute host dir>   host root(s) tried as <dir>/<entry> when no committed candidate exists (read-only allow-list applies)
#   alias     M  <entry>  <BASE-rel committed path>     the entry is committed under another name (reason cites the README line)
#   aliaspfx  M  <entry prefix/>  <BASE-rel committed root/>    same, for every entry under a prefix
#   abs2c     M  <absolute prefix/>  <BASE-rel committed root, `.` = BASE>   absolute entries whose committed copy lives under a root
#   xform     M  <entry | prefix/ | *>  bom-crlf       the committed copy is a documented LF/BOM-stripped copy; compare after re-adding UTF-8 BOM + CRLF
#   hxform    M  <entry | prefix/ | *>  strip-ansi-dsn  the recorded hash is of the committed-style stripped copy (ANSI colour codes removed and `postgres://` lines
#                                                         dropped, the strip() of run2/qualification-2/qual.sh.txt:17); the host original is hashed raw AND after that strip
#   notret    M  <entry | prefix/ | *>  -              only applies when the host file is ABSENT; otherwise the host file is hashed as usual
#   super     M  <entry>  <successor manifest>:<entry>   the recorded hash was superseded; accepted only if the host file now equals the
# A rule is cited in the output note as map:L<line>. Every non-default rule carries the README line that documents it.
# ---- manifests that the name rule (SHA256SUMS | *sha256* | *.sha, case-insensitive) does not pick up -------------------------------
